# surtgis_core::resample - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/surtgis-core/0.17.0/surtgis_core/resample/index.html

## Expand description

Raster resampling: align a raster to a reference grid.

Resamples a source raster to match the exact grid (origin, cell size, dimensions) of a reference raster. Essential for stacking rasters from different sources (e.g., Copernicus DEM at 30m + Sentinel-2 at 10m).

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Resample](https://docs.rs/enum.ResampleMethod.html)- Method
- Interpolation method for resampling.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [resample_](https://docs.rs/fn.resample_to_grid.html)- to_ - grid
- Resample a raster to match the grid of a reference raster.

# surtgis_core::streaming - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/surtgis-core/0.17.0/surtgis_core/streaming/index.html

## Expand description

Streaming processor for window-based raster algorithms.

Processes rasters strip-by-strip with bounded memory, enabling arbitrarily large DEMs for algorithms that only need a local window.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Strip](https://docs.rs/struct.StripProcessor.html)- Processor
- Streaming processor that reads and writes GeoTIFF strip-by-strip.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Window](https://docs.rs/trait.WindowAlgorithm.html)- Algorithm
- Trait for algorithms that operate on a moving window.

# surtgis_core::tiling - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/surtgis-core/0.17.0/surtgis_core/tiling/index.html

## Expand description

2-D tile iteration with overlap for windowed processing.

[ TileGrid](https://docs.rs/struct.TileGrid.html) partitions a raster grid into fixed-size tiles and
yields, for each tile, both its

**core**extent (the cells the tile owns — cores never overlap and together cover the grid exactly) and its

**read**extent (core expanded by

`overlap` cells on every
side, clamped to the grid). Algorithms read the expanded window,
compute, and write back only the core — the standard halo pattern
for kernels, embeddings, and seam-free tiled inference.This is the 2-D counterpart of [ StripProcessor](https://docs.rs/streaming/struct.StripProcessor.html),
which handles the 1-D (row strip) case with file-backed I/O.

```
use surtgis_core::tiling::TileGrid;
let grid = TileGrid::new(1000, 1500, 256, 16);
for tile in grid {
    // read tile.read_* window, compute, write tile.core_* cells
    assert!(tile.read_rows <= 256 + 2 * 16);
}
```

---

# surtgis_core::vector - Rust

Vector data structures and operations.

Supports reading features from multiple formats:

- **Shapefile**(requires- `shapefile`feature)

Use [ read_vector](https://docs.rs/fn.read_vector.html) for automatic format detection by file extension,
or call the format-specific readers directly.

# kigumi-schema 0.1.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/kigumi-schema/0.1.0

The projections: from a `ResolvedModel` to Postgres DDL and an agnostic UI contract (JSON).

Same source of truth → multiple outputs. The UI contract carries visibility/readonly rules as
a portable [`Domain`] JSON AST — the frontend evaluates them client-side from data, never an
eval'd string, and they are the SAME domains the server compiles to SQL.

# kigumi_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/kigumi-core/^0.1.0/

## Expand description

Kigumi core: the inspectable metamodel + the module versioning model.

Difference from Odoo (see `docs/ANALISI_ODOO19.md`): a model definition is NOT
a class synthesized at runtime with `type()`, but inspectable static data;
extension is a VERIFIED MERGE, not a global monkey-patch; dependencies between
modules have verified VERSION RANGES (Odoo does not have them — see `docs/VERSIONING.md`).

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [inventory](https://docs.rs/inventory/0.3.24/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/inventory/index.html);

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Acl](https://docs.rs/struct.Acl.html)
- Model-level access grant for one group (the `ir.model.access`analog).
- [AclRegistration](https://docs.rs/struct.AclRegistration.html)
- Registration of a module’s ACLs (emitted by `register_acls!`). Compile-time security data; M6 adds a DB-backed loader on top, but the in-code registry stays the bootstrap/default source.
- [Action](https://docs.rs/struct.ActionInput.html)- Input
- Read-only view of the record an action runs on (its current stored values), with typed accessors.
- [Action](https://docs.rs/struct.ActionOutcome.html)- Outcome
- What an action produces: field updates to apply, plus an optional “assign field = next_value(code)” directive resolved by the persistence layer (which can call the sequence engine).
- [Action](https://docs.rs/struct.ActionRegistration.html)- Registration
- Registration of an action by (model, name), emitted by `register_action!`.`groups`(if non-empty) restricts who may run it, on top of the model’s Write ACL + record rules.
- [Compute](https://docs.rs/struct.ComputeInput.html)- Input
- Read-only view of a record (its own fields + its One2many children), passed to a compute
function. Same-record computes read `int`/`float`/…; aggregate computes read`children`/`sum_float`.
- [Compute](https://docs.rs/struct.ComputeRegistration.html)- Registration
- Registration of a compute function by name (emitted by `register_compute!`).
- [Condition](https://docs.rs/struct.Condition.html)
- A single leaf condition `field <op> value`.
- [Constraint](https://docs.rs/struct.ConstraintRegistration.html)- Registration
- Registration of a constraint on a model, evaluated when any of `fields`is written (an empty`fields`runs on every write). Emitted by`register_constraint!`.
- [Constraint](https://docs.rs/struct.ConstraintViolation.html)- Violation
- A constraint violation: the failing rule’s message plus the fields the rule DECLARED as its triggers — the fields a form should highlight. Empty for an unconditional (whole-record) rule.
- [Ctx](https://docs.rs/struct.Ctx.html)
- Evaluation context: who is acting, and whether checks are bypassed.
- [Delegated](https://docs.rs/struct.DelegatedField.html)- Field
- A field a child transparently exposes from its `_inherits`parent: the parent’s`FieldDef``via`FK column the read subquery / write UPDATE pivots on.
- [External](https://docs.rs/struct.ExternalTable.html)- Table
- A model whose table is owned OUTSIDE the metamodel (e.g. the auth subsystem’s `kigumi_user`, or a SQL view): registered so it is resolved/served like any model, but EXCLUDED from migration — the metamodel never creates or alters its table. Odoo’s`_auto = False`. Emitted by`register_external!`.
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldBuilder.html)- Builder
- Fluent builder for a single condition.
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldDef.html)- Def
- Definition of a single field.
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldExtension.html)- Extension
- Registration of a field extension (emitted by `#[extend]`).
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldGroup.html)- Group
- A titled group of scalar fields, laid out in two columns. `title`is optional (a lead group with no heading is common for the identity fields).
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldGroupRegistration.html)- Group - Registration
- Field-level access restriction (D6 / Odoo’s `Field.groups`): the groups required to access one`model.field`. Registered out-of-band (emitted by`#[field(groups = "...")]`) so it adds no column to the metamodel and no churn to existing`FieldDef`literals — the same side-registry pattern as external tables. Read AND write are gated by the same set, at the DB boundary.
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldSlot.html)- Slot
- A field placed in a group. `full`makes it span both columns — use it for relations, long text (Html), images, and the primary name.
- [Form](https://docs.rs/struct.FormView.html)- View
- A model’s form layout. Emitted by `register_view!`.
- [Inherits](https://docs.rs/struct.InheritsRegistration.html)- Registration
- Delegation inheritance (Odoo’s `_inherits`):`model`carries a required Many2one`via`to`parent`and transparently exposes the parent’s stored scalar fields (read via the FK, written through to the parent). Emitted by`#[model(inherits = "parent", via = "fk")]`. The`via`FK is an ordinary field the model declares — this only records the delegation, so no`ModelDescriptor`/`FieldDef`churn.
- [Mailed](https://docs.rs/struct.MailedRegistration.html)- Registration
- A model that opts INTO the mail subsystem (chatter): it gains a thread of `mail.message`s, followers and activities, addressed by the polymorphic`(res_model, res_id)`link. Emitted by`register_mailed!`. Unlike Odoo’s 5118-line`mail.thread`mixin, this is a one-line compile-time marker the framework iterates — to gate the chatter API and to clean up the thread on delete.
- [Migration](https://docs.rs/struct.MigrationTarget.html)- Target
- One model to migrate, with the owning module’s name + version (for the migration ledger).
- [Model](https://docs.rs/struct.ModelDescriptor.html)- Descriptor
- Descriptor of a model as defined by ONE module (the “base”).
- [Model](https://docs.rs/struct.ModelRegistration.html)- Registration
- Registration of a base model (emitted by `#[model]`).
- [Module](https://docs.rs/struct.ModuleDep.html)- Dep
- Dependency on another module, with a SemVer version constraint (e.g. “^1.2”).
- [Module](https://docs.rs/struct.ModuleManifest.html)- Manifest
- Manifest of a module. Declarative data, validated at build/install time.
- [Module](https://docs.rs/struct.ModuleRegistration.html)- Registration
- Registration of a module manifest (emitted by `register_module!`).`crate_path`is the Rust module path of the registering crate (`module_path!()`), used to map a model — whose own registration carries`module_path!()`— back to its owning manifest (name + version).
- [Notebook](https://docs.rs/struct.NotebookPage.html)- Page
- A notebook page (tab) below the sheet, usually a One2many relation or grouped secondary fields.
- [Readonly](https://docs.rs/struct.ReadonlyFieldRegistration.html)- Field - Registration
- A stored field declared read-only: shown in the UI contract as `readonly`and rejected by the write path (like a computed field), even though it is not computed. Emitted by`#[field(readonly)]`. Used for materialized values a service method maintains (e.g. on-hand) — visible, never hand-edited.
- [Record](https://docs.rs/struct.RecordRule.html)- Rule
- Row-level rule (the `ir.rule`analog).`groups`empty = global (applies to everyone).
- [Record](https://docs.rs/struct.RecordRuleRegistration.html)- Rule - Registration
- Registration of a module’s record rules (emitted by `register_rules!`).
- [Related](https://docs.rs/struct.RelatedRegistration.html)- Registration
- A related field (Odoo `related=`): a NON-stored, read-only mirror of a value reached by following a relational`path`(e.g.`order_id.currency_id`). Registered out-of-band (emitted by`#[field(related = "...")]`) so it adds no column to the metamodel — the value is resolved at read time by a correlated subquery over the path. The field’s declared kind must match the path target.
- [Report](https://docs.rs/struct.ReportRegistration.html)- Registration
- Registration of a report by (model, name), emitted by `register_report!`.`name`is the URL segment (e.g. “quotation”);`title`is the human label used in the contract and the download filename.
- [Resolved](https://docs.rs/struct.ResolvedModel.html)- Model
- RESOLVED descriptor: base + all extensions merged and validated. This is the point — absent in Odoo — where the final definition is materializable.
- [Sequence](https://docs.rs/struct.SequenceRegistration.html)- Registration
- A module’s document-numbering sequence (emitted by `register_sequence!`): declared next to the action that consumes it, ensured at migrate — an existing sequence keeps its counter.`module`is diagnostic only (a cross-module code collision is reported with both names).
- [Sql](https://docs.rs/struct.Sql.html)
- Compiled SQL: a boolean expression plus its ordered bound parameters.
- [Tracked](https://docs.rs/struct.TrackedFieldRegistration.html)- Field - Registration
- A field whose changes are tracked in the chatter (Odoo’s `tracking=True`). When a write changes it on a mailed model, the write path records a`notification`message + a typed`mail.tracking`row (old → new). Emitted by`#[field(tracked)]`. Compile-time, not runtime`track_visibility`.
- [Transient](https://docs.rs/struct.TransientRegistration.html)- Registration
- A model whose rows are ephemeral (Odoo’s `TransientModel`): a wizard scratchpad with its own table, served and secured like any model, but periodically garbage-collected by age. Emitted by`register_transient!`. A transient model declares a nullable`create_date Datetime`; migration gives that column a`DEFAULT now()`so every insert is timestamped and the GC cron can reclaim it.
- [Wizard](https://docs.rs/struct.WizardContext.html)- Context
- The records a wizard is opened against (Odoo’s `active_model`/`active_id`/`active_ids`context).
- [Wizard](https://docs.rs/struct.WizardRegistration.html)- Registration
- Registration of a wizard (emitted by `register_wizard!`): binds a transient model to its`default_get`. The model must also be`register_transient!`-marked (so its rows are GC’d).

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Domain](https://docs.rs/enum.Domain.html)
- A filter expression. Combine with `and`/`or`/`not`.
- [Domain](https://docs.rs/enum.DomainError.html)- Error
- [Field](https://docs.rs/enum.FieldKind.html)- Kind
- Logical type of a field. From this we derive the SQL type, UI widget, and API type.
- [Operation](https://docs.rs/enum.Operation.html)
- A CRUD operation subject to access control.
- [Operator](https://docs.rs/enum.Operator.html)
- [Resolution](https://docs.rs/enum.ResolutionError.html)- Error
- [Rule](https://docs.rs/enum.RuleDomain.html)- Domain
- The domain source of a `RecordRule``Static`(a thunk, because a`Domain``Owned`, holding a domain parsed at load time. The engine treats both identically — only where the domain comes from differs, so static and DB rules merge into one list with no special-casing.
- [Value](https://docs.rs/enum.Value.html)
- A scalar (or list) literal used on the right-hand side of a condition.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [FRAMEWORK_](https://docs.rs/constant.FRAMEWORK_VERSION.html)- VERSION
- Framework SemVer version (= workspace version). Modules compare it
against their own compatibility range via `check_compat`

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Model](https://docs.rs/trait.Model.html)
- Implemented by every model. In the walking skeleton it is written by hand;
in phase 2 it is generated by the `#[model]`proc-macro.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [action_](https://docs.rs/fn.action_for.html)- for
- Looks up a registered action by model + name.
- [actions_](https://docs.rs/fn.actions_for.html)- for
- All actions registered on `model`(for the UI contract, so a form can render its action buttons).
- [check_](https://docs.rs/fn.check_access.html)- access
- Returns true if `ctx`may perform`op`on`model`. Access is granted if ANY of the user’s groups grants it (union semantics, like Odoo). Superuser is always allowed.
- [check_](https://docs.rs/fn.check_compat.html)- compat
- Verifies that `manifest`is compatible with the provided framework version. This is the check Odoo does NOT do: there a “19.0” module runs (or breaks) on any 19.x.
- [check_](https://docs.rs/fn.check_constraints.html)- constraints
- Runs the model’s constraints over a just-written record (`values`+ its`children`).`changed`is the set of written field names, or`None`on create (every constraint runs). A constraint runs when it is unconditional (empty`fields`), on create, or when one of its trigger`fields`was written. Returns the first violation (message + the rule’s declared fields), which the caller maps to a typed error that rolls back the tx.
- [compute_](https://docs.rs/fn.compute_fn.html)- fn
- Looks up a registered compute function by its declared name.
- [compute_](https://docs.rs/fn.compute_on_read.html)- on_ - read
- Evaluates the model’s NON-stored computed fields (Odoo `compute=`without`store=True`) over a record’s`values`at READ time, returning the (name, value) pairs to inject into the projection. These have no column and are never written — they are derived on every read. Same-record:`children`is empty, so a function reads the record’s own scalar fields plus any related / delegated values already present in`values`(both are read alongside the columns), not its One2many children.
- [compute_](https://docs.rs/fn.compute_stored.html)- stored
- Fills `values`with the result of each stored computed field whose function is registered, given the record’s own fields and its One2many`children`(for aggregate computes). Computes from a snapshot taken BEFORE writing any result, so computes read the inputs (chained compute-on-compute is not ordered — out of scope).
- [computed_](https://docs.rs/fn.computed_fields.html)- fields
- Names of the model’s stored computed fields that have a registered function.
- [delegated_](https://docs.rs/fn.delegated_fields.html)- fields
- The fields `model`delegates to its`_inherits`parent (empty if it is not a child). Each is read via the parent through the`via`FK; the child does NOT have a column for it. A name the child also declares (an intentional shadow, e.g.`product.product.active`over`product.template.active`) is excluded — the child’s own column wins and the parent’s is not delegated.
- [external_](https://docs.rs/fn.external_tables.html)- tables
- Names of models whose tables the metamodel must NOT migrate (owned externally).
- [field_](https://docs.rs/fn.field_accessible.html)- accessible
- Whether `ctx`may access (read or write)`model.field`. Default-allow when the field has no group restriction; superuser always allowed; otherwise the caller must be in at least one required group. Mirrors Odoo, which gates read and write by the same`Field.groups`set at the ORM boundary.
- [field_](https://docs.rs/fn.field_is_readonly.html)- is_ - readonly
- Whether `model`.`field`is declared`#[field(readonly)]`.
- [field_](https://docs.rs/fn.field_required_groups.html)- required_ - groups
- The groups required to access `model.field`, or None when the field is unrestricted. Delegation- aware (`_inherits`): a restriction on an inherited field lives on the PARENT model, so when the field is not restricted directly on`model`we fall back to the parent — otherwise an inherited field would expose its restricted value through the child (read/order/filter). Recurses the chain. Shadow-aware: a name the child declares as its OWN column (e.g.`product.product.active`over`product.template.active`) does NOT borrow the parent’s restriction — only genuinely delegated fields fall back, so a group added to the parent never silently gates the child’s own column.
- [has_](https://docs.rs/fn.has_constraints.html)- constraints
- True iff the model has any registered constraint — a cheap gate before the in-transaction re-read
that `check_constraints`
- [has_](https://docs.rs/fn.has_read_computes.html)- read_ - computes
- True iff the model has any NON-stored computed field (a cheap gate before doing the extra decode
that `compute_on_read`
- [inherits_](https://docs.rs/fn.inherits_of.html)- of
- The `(parent, via)`a model delegates to, or None if it is not an`_inherits`child.
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_mailed.html)- mailed
- Whether `model`has a mail thread (chatter enabled).
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_transient.html)- transient
- Whether `model`is transient (its rows are garbage-collected by age).
- [json_](https://docs.rs/fn.json_string.html)- string
- JSON-escapes `s`and wraps it in double quotes. Shared by domain and UI-contract serialization so every string in the emitted JSON is escaped consistently (no broken-out quotes).
- [mailed_](https://docs.rs/fn.mailed_models.html)- models
- Names of all models that opted into the mail subsystem.
- [migration_](https://docs.rs/fn.migration_plan.html)- plan
- The full migration plan, TOPOLOGICALLY SORTED by Many2one FK dependencies (a model’s FK targets — e.g. res.currency/res.partner for res.company — are created before the referencing table). Self-references are ignored (a table may reference itself in its own CREATE); a genuine FK cycle between two tables is an error. Ties break by (module dependency order, model name) for determinism. Each target carries its owning module’s name + version for the migration ledger.
- [module_](https://docs.rs/fn.module_closure.html)- closure
- A module plus its full transitive dependency closure, in dependency order (dependencies first) —
the set to install when installing `name`. Errors if`name`(or a dependency) is not a linked module, or the module graph is invalid.
- [module_](https://docs.rs/fn.module_of.html)- of
- The name of the module that owns `model`, via the model’s registration crate_path → manifest mapping (the same hook`migration_plan`uses). Used to gate migration/serving by installed module.
- [record_](https://docs.rs/fn.record_rule_domain.html)- rule_ - domain
- Combines the record rules applicable to (`op`,`model`,`ctx`) into a single restricting`Domain``None`when nothing restricts (superuser, or no applicable rule).
- [registered_](https://docs.rs/fn.registered_acls.html)- acls
- All ACLs registered across linked modules (the union a server enforces).
- [registered_](https://docs.rs/fn.registered_group_names.html)- group_ - names
- Distinct group names referenced by any registered ACL or record rule — the catalog’s known
groups (the source for seeding the read-only `res.groups`list). Sorted, deterministic.
- [registered_](https://docs.rs/fn.registered_model_names.html)- model_ - names
- Names of all models registered in the catalog (sorted, deterministic).
- [registered_](https://docs.rs/fn.registered_rules.html)- rules
- All record rules registered across linked modules.
- [registered_](https://docs.rs/fn.registered_sequences.html)- sequences
- All sequences registered across linked modules.
- [related_](https://docs.rs/fn.related_path.html)- path
- The relational path a related field mirrors, or None if `field`is not a related field.
- [report_](https://docs.rs/fn.report_for.html)- for
- Looks up a registered report by model + name.
- [reports_](https://docs.rs/fn.reports_for.html)- for
- All reports registered on `model`(for the UI contract, so a form can offer its “Print” buttons).
- [resolve](https://docs.rs/fn.resolve.html)
- Merges the base with the module extensions. Conflicts are errors.
- [resolve_](https://docs.rs/fn.resolve_all_registered.html)- all_ - registered
- Resolves every registered model (base + extensions). The bridge from the catalog to a server or any consumer that needs the full set of models.
- [resolve_](https://docs.rs/fn.resolve_module_set.html)- module_ - set
- Resolves a set of modules: checks framework compatibility, that every dependency exists with a satisfying SemVer version, that there are no duplicate names and no cycles. Returns the modules in dependency (topological) order — what Odoo computes implicitly.
- [resolve_](https://docs.rs/fn.resolve_modules.html)- modules
- Resolves every module registered in the catalog: framework compatibility, dependency
version ranges, no duplicates, no cycles — returning them in dependency order.
The validation `resolve_module_set`does is exactly what Odoo’s`depends`cannot express.
- [resolve_](https://docs.rs/fn.resolve_registered.html)- registered
- Resolves a model from the CATALOG: registered base + all auto-registered extensions, merged (with conflict checks) and validated. No wiring: modules auto-register.
- [tracked_](https://docs.rs/fn.tracked_fields.html)- fields
- The names of `model`’s tracked fields (changes recorded in the chatter on write).
- [transient_](https://docs.rs/fn.transient_models.html)- models
- Names of all transient (ephemeral / wizard) models.
- [validate_](https://docs.rs/fn.validate_depends.html)- depends
- Verifies that each `depends`points to an existing field (first segment of the path). Antidote to Odoo’s silent N+1: a broken dependency is an error, not a runtime bug.
- [validate_](https://docs.rs/fn.validate_depends_with_extra.html)- depends_ - with_ - extra
- Like `validate_depends``extra`lists additional valid first-segment names — the`_inherits`delegated fields, which have no column on`m`yet are readable on the record (so an on-read compute may depend on, e.g., the inherited`name`). The registry passes the delegated names here.
- [view_](https://docs.rs/fn.view_for.html)- for
- The registered form view for `model`, if any (else the frontend applies a smart default layout).
- [wizard_](https://docs.rs/fn.wizard_for.html)- for
- Looks up a registered wizard by model name.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Action](https://docs.rs/type.ActionFn.html)- Fn
- A registered action: a pure transition function. Guards (e.g. “only a draft”) live in the body
and return `Err(message)`to refuse the transition.
- [Children](https://docs.rs/type.Children.html)
- One2many children grouped by the o2m field name (each child is its own field→value map).
- [Compute](https://docs.rs/type.ComputeFn.html)- Fn
- A registered compute function.
- [Constraint](https://docs.rs/type.ConstraintFn.html)- Fn
- A constraint over a just-written record: returns `Err(message)`to reject (and roll back) the write.
- [Report](https://docs.rs/type.ReportFn.html)- Fn
- Renders a record — with its inlined One2many children, exactly as `find_one_secured`returns it — to a complete HTML document. Pure: no DB access and no recompute; it reads only the fields present.
- [Wizard](https://docs.rs/type.WizardDefaultGet.html)- Default - Get
- Computes a wizard’s seed field values from the context (Odoo’s `default_get`). Pure in v1 (no DB reads); DB-backed defaults are a later extension done by a dedicated open service method.

---

# kigumi_schema - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/kigumi-schema/0.1.0/target-redirect/kigumi_schema/

## Expand description

The projections: from a `ResolvedModel` to Postgres DDL and an agnostic UI contract (JSON).

Same source of truth → multiple outputs. The UI contract carries visibility/readonly rules as
a portable [ Domain](https://docs.rs/kigumi-core/0.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/kigumi_core/domain/enum.Domain.html) JSON AST — the frontend evaluates them client-side from data, never an
eval’d string, and they are the SAME domains the server compiles to SQL.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldRule.html)- Rule
- A dynamic UI rule bound to a field: when `domain`holds for a record, the field becomes invisible/readonly. The domain is a thunk because a`Domain`

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [openapi](https://docs.rs/fn.openapi.html)
- Builds a pretty-printed OpenAPI 3.1 document describing `models`.
- [pg_](https://docs.rs/fn.pg_add_column_type.html)- add_ - column_ - type
- The column TYPE plus its foreign-key reference for an additive `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN`— the subset of`to_ddl`’s column spec WITHOUT NOT NULL / UNIQUE / CHECK / DEFAULT, so it is safe to add to a populated table (the column is simply NULL on existing rows; required-ness is enforced at the write layer).`None`for kinds with no own column (One2many / Many2many).
- [pg_](https://docs.rs/fn.pg_column_type.html)- column_ - type
- Postgres SQL type for a field with a column.
The Postgres column type for a field kind — used by `to_ddl`and by the runtime custom-field`ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN`. Empty string for kinds that have no own column (One2many/Many2many).
- [to_ddl](https://docs.rs/fn.to_ddl.html)
- Generates the `CREATE TABLE`. Non-stored computed fields and one2many produce no columns.
- [to_](https://docs.rs/fn.to_ui_contract.html)- ui_ - contract
- Agnostic UI contract: JSON consumable by ANY frontend. Computed fields are readonly; dynamic
`invisible_when`/`readonly_when`rules are emitted as portable domain ASTs.

---

[57](#57)pub fn to_ddl(m: &ResolvedModel) -> String {
[59](#59)    let mut lines = vec!["  id bigserial PRIMARY KEY".to_string()];
[60](#60)    for f in m.fields.iter().filter(|f| f.has_column()) {
[61](#61)        let mut col = format!("  {} {}", f.name, pg_type(&f.kind));
[62](#62)        match f.kind {
[63](#63)            FieldKind::Many2one { target } => col.push_str(&format!(" REFERENCES {}(id)", table_of(target))),
[64](#64)            FieldKind::Image => col.push_str(" REFERENCES kigumi_attachment(id)"),
[66](#66)            _ => {}
[67](#67)        }
[68](#68)        if f.required {
[69](#69)            col.push_str(" NOT NULL");
[70](#70)        }
[71](#71)        if f.unique {
[72](#72)            col.push_str(" UNIQUE");
[73](#73)        }
[74](#74)        if let Some(expr) = f.check {
[76](#76)            col.push_str(&format!(" CHECK ({expr})"));
[77](#77)        }
[78](#78)        lines.push(col);
[79](#79)    }
[80](#80)    format!("CREATE TABLE {} (\n{}\n);", m.table, lines.join(",\n"))

[126](#126)pub fn to_ui_contract(m: &ResolvedModel, rules: &[FieldRule]) -> Result<String, DomainError> {
[133](#133)    for r in rules {
[134](#134)        (r.domain)().validate(m)?;
[135](#135)    }
[136](#136)    let emit = |f: &FieldDef, readonly: bool| -> String {
[139](#139)        let mut parts = vec![
[140](#140)            format!("\"name\": {}", json_string(f.name)),
[141](#141)            format!("\"label\": {}", json_string(f.label)),
[142](#142)            format!("\"widget\": \"{}\"", widget(&f.kind)),
[143](#143)            format!("\"required\": {}", f.required),
[144](#144)            format!("\"readonly\": {readonly}"),
[145](#145)        ];
[146](#146)        if let FieldKind::Selection(opts) = &f.kind {
[147](#147)            let items: Vec<String> = opts
[148](#148)                .iter()
[149](#149)                .map(|(v, l)| format!("{{ \"value\": {}, \"label\": {} }}", json_string(v), json_string(l)))
[150](#150)                .collect();
[151](#151)            parts.push(format!("\"options\": [{}]", items.join(", ")));
[152](#152)        }
[153](#153)        match &f.kind {
[154](#154)            FieldKind::Many2one { target } => {
[155](#155)                parts.push(format!("\"relation\": {}", json_string(target)));
[156](#156)            }
[157](#157)            FieldKind::One2many { target, inverse } => {
[158](#158)                parts.push(format!("\"relation\": {}", json_string(target)));
[159](#159)                parts.push(format!("\"inverse\": {}", json_string(inverse)));
[160](#160)            }
[161](#161)            _ => {}
[162](#162)        }
[163](#163)        if let Some(d) = f.default {
[164](#164)            parts.push(format!("\"default\": {}", json_string(d)));
[165](#165)        }
[166](#166)        if let Some(j) = rule_json(rules, f.name, UiRule::Invisible) {
[167](#167)            parts.push(format!("\"invisible_when\": {j}"));
[168](#168)        }
[169](#169)        if let Some(j) = rule_json(rules, f.name, UiRule::Readonly) {
[170](#170)            parts.push(format!("\"readonly_when\": {j}"));
[171](#171)        }
[172](#172)        format!("    {{ {} }}", parts.join(", "))
[173](#173)    };
[174](#174)    let mut fields: Vec<String> = m
[175](#175)        .fields

[177](#177)        .map(|f| {
[178](#178)            let readonly = f.is_computed() || related_path(m.name, f.name).is_some() || field_is_readonly(m.name, f.name);
[181](#181)            emit(f, readonly)
[182](#182)        })
[183](#183)        .collect();
[184](#184)    let delegated = delegated_fields(m.name).unwrap_or_default();
[187](#187)    for d in &delegated {
[188](#188)        fields.push(emit(&d.def, false));
[189](#189)    }
[190](#190)    let list_friendly = |kind: &FieldKind| {
[196](#196)        !matches!(
[197](#197)            kind,
[198](#198)            FieldKind::Image | FieldKind::Html | FieldKind::One2many { .. } | FieldKind::Many2many { .. }
[199](#199)        )
[200](#200)    };
[201](#201)    let col_json = |name: &str, label: &str, kind: &FieldKind| {

[203](#203)            "    {{ \"name\": {}, \"label\": {}, \"widget\": \"{}\" }}",

[205](#205)            json_string(label),
[206](#206)            widget(kind)
[207](#207)        )
[208](#208)    };
[209](#209)    const MAX_LIST_COLUMNS: usize = 8;
[210](#210)    let columns: Vec<String> = if let Some(v) = view_for(m.name) {
[211](#211)        let mut cols = Vec::new();
[212](#212)        for g in v.groups {
[213](#213)            for s in g.fields {
[214](#214)                if cols.len() >= MAX_LIST_COLUMNS {
[215](#215)                    break;
[216](#216)                }
[217](#217)                if field_required_groups(m.name, s.name).is_some() {
[218](#218)                    continue;
[219](#219)                }
[220](#220)                if let Some(f) = m.fields.iter().find(|f| f.name == s.name) {
[223](#223)                    if list_friendly(&f.kind) {
[224](#224)                        cols.push(col_json(f.name, f.label, &f.kind));
[225](#225)                    }
[226](#226)                } else if let Some(d) = delegated.iter().find(|d| d.def.name == s.name) {
[227](#227)                    if list_friendly(&d.def.kind) {
[228](#228)                        cols.push(col_json(d.def.name, d.def.label, &d.def.kind));
[229](#229)                    }
[230](#230)                }
[231](#231)            }
[232](#232)        }
[233](#233)        cols
[234](#234)    } else {
[235](#235)        let mut cols: Vec<String> = m
[236](#236)            .fields
[237](#237)            .iter()
[238](#238)            .filter(|f| {
[239](#239)                (f.has_column() || f.is_computed() || related_path(m.name, f.name).is_some())
[240](#240)                    && list_friendly(&f.kind)
[241](#241)                    && field_required_groups(m.name, f.name).is_none()
[242](#242)            })
[243](#243)            .take(MAX_LIST_COLUMNS)
[244](#244)            .map(|f| col_json(f.name, f.label, &f.kind))
[245](#245)            .collect();
[246](#246)        for d in &delegated {
[247](#247)            if cols.len() < MAX_LIST_COLUMNS && list_friendly(&d.def.kind) {
[248](#248)                cols.push(col_json(d.def.name, d.def.label, &d.def.kind));
[249](#249)            }
[250](#250)        }
[251](#251)        cols
[252](#252)    };
[253](#253)
[254](#254)    let actions: Vec<String> = actions_for(m.name)
[257](#257)        .iter()
[258](#258)        .map(|a| {
[259](#259)            let groups: Vec<String> = a.groups.iter().map(|g| json_string(g)).collect();
[260](#260)            format!(

[262](#262)                json_string(a.name),
[263](#263)                groups.join(", ")

[265](#265)        })
[266](#266)        .collect();

[268](#268)    let reports: Vec<String> = reports_for(m.name)
[270](#270)        .iter()
[271](#271)        .map(|r| format!("    {{ \"name\": {}, \"title\": {} }}", json_string(r.name), json_string(r.title)))
[272](#272)        .collect();
[273](#273)
[274](#274)    let view = match view_for(m.name) {
[277](#277)        None => "null".to_string(),
[278](#278)        Some(v) => {
[279](#279)            let groups: Vec<String> = v
[280](#280)                .groups
[281](#281)                .iter()
[282](#282)                .map(|g| {
[283](#283)                    let slots: Vec<String> = g
[284](#284)                        .fields
[285](#285)                        .iter()
[286](#286)                        .map(|f| format!("{{ \"name\": {}, \"full\": {} }}", json_string(f.name), f.full))
[287](#287)                        .collect();
[288](#288)                    let title = g.title.map(json_string).unwrap_or_else(|| "null".to_string());
[289](#289)                    format!("{{ \"title\": {}, \"fields\": [{}] }}", title, slots.join(", "))
[290](#290)                })
[291](#291)                .collect();
[292](#292)            let pages: Vec<String> = v
[293](#293)                .pages
[294](#294)                .iter()
[295](#295)                .map(|p| {
[296](#296)                    let pf: Vec<String> = p.fields.iter().map(|f| json_string(f)).collect();
[297](#297)                    format!("{{ \"title\": {}, \"fields\": [{}] }}", json_string(p.title), pf.join(", "))
[298](#298)                })
[299](#299)                .collect();
[300](#300)            format!("{{ \"groups\": [{}], \"pages\": [{}] }}", groups.join(", "), pages.join(", "))
[301](#301)        }
[302](#302)    };
[303](#303)
[304](#304)    Ok(format!(
[305](#305)        "{{\n  \"model\": {},\n  \"type\": \"form\",\n  \"mailed\": {},\n  \"fields\": [\n{}\n  ],\n  \"list\": {{ \"columns\": [\n{}\n  ] }},\n  \"actions\": [\n{}\n  ],\n  \"reports\": [\n{}\n  ],\n  \"view\": {}\n}}",
[306](#306)        json_string(m.name),
[307](#307)        is_mailed(m.name),

[309](#309)        columns.join(",\n"),

# pg_add_column_type in kigumi_schema - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/kigumi-schema/0.1.0/kigumi_schema/fn.pg_add_column_type.html

## Expand description

The column TYPE plus its foreign-key reference for an additive `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` — the subset
of `to_ddl`’s column spec WITHOUT NOT NULL / UNIQUE / CHECK / DEFAULT, so it is safe to add to a
populated table (the column is simply NULL on existing rows; required-ness is enforced at the write
layer). `None` for kinds with no own column (One2many / Many2many).

---

# pg_column_type in kigumi_schema - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/kigumi-schema/0.1.0/kigumi_schema/fn.pg_column_type.html

## Expand description

Postgres SQL type for a field with a column.
The Postgres column type for a field kind — used by `to_ddl` and by the runtime custom-field
`ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN`. Empty string for kinds that have no own column (One2many/Many2many).

# to_ui_contract in kigumi_schema - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/kigumi-schema/0.1.0/kigumi_schema/fn.to_ui_contract.html

```
pub fn to_ui_contract(
    m: &
```
[ResolvedModel](https://docs.rs/kigumi-core/0.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/kigumi_core/metamodel/struct.ResolvedModel.html),
    rules: &[[FieldRule](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldRule.html)],
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html), [DomainError](https://docs.rs/kigumi-core/0.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/kigumi_core/domain/enum.DomainError.html)>## Expand description

Agnostic UI contract: JSON consumable by ANY frontend. Computed fields are readonly; dynamic
`invisible_when` / `readonly_when` rules are emitted as portable domain ASTs.

Returns an error if any rule references an unknown/invalid field — UI rules are validated, not
discovered broken in production (the Odoo `attrs`/xpath failure mode).
ponytail: JSON built by hand (zero-dep). Switch to serde in phase 5.

# nn_rust 0.1.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/nn_rust/0.1.0

# Rust Neural Network Library

A simple neural network library written in Rust, designed for learning, experimentation, and building small AI systems from scratch. Includes training utilities, activation functions, and example projects.

## Features

- Fully implemented feedforward neural networks
- Backpropagation with gradient descent
- Modular layer system
- Common activation functions (ReLU, Sigmoid, Tanh)
- CPU-based training (no external ML dependencies)
- Example binaries demonstrating learning tasks

## Getting Started

### Clone the repository

```
#Build just the Library
```
## Running Examples

This project includes several demo binaries located in `src/bin/`.

```
```
Videos of the Neural Network learning regression and classification:

## Usage as a Library

Add this to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = {  = "../NeuralNetworkRust" }
```
Example code:

```
;
{

  ;
}
```
## Motivation

This project was built to deeply understand how neural networks work under the hood, including forward propagation, backpropagation, and optimization without relying on high-level ML frameworks.

# rand - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rand/^0.10.1/

## Expand description

Random-number generators and samplers

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick Start

```
// rand::random() supports many common types:
println!("Uniform i8 sample: {}", match rand::random() {
    0i8 => "zero",
    i if i > 0 => "positive",
    _ => "negative",
});
// Ranged sampling:
use std::f32::consts::PI;
println!("Angle: {} degrees", rand::random_range(-PI..PI));
```
See also [The Book: Quick Start](https://rust-random.github.io/book/quick-start.html).

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

# flate2 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/flate2/^1.1.9/

## Expand description

A DEFLATE-based stream compression/decompression library

This library provides support for compression and decompression of DEFLATE-based streams:

- the DEFLATE format itself
- the zlib format
- gzip

These three formats are all closely related and largely only differ in their headers/footers. This crate has three types in each submodule for dealing with these three formats.

[§](https://docs.rs#implementation)Implementation

In addition to supporting three formats, this crate supports several different
backends, controlled through this crate’s *features flags*:

-
`default`, or`rust_backend`- this implementation currently uses the`miniz_oxide`crate which is a port of`miniz.c`to Rust. This feature does not require a C compiler, and only uses safe Rust code.Note that the `rust_backend`feature may at some point be switched to use`zlib-rs`, and that`miniz_oxide`should be used explicitly if this is not desired.
-
`zlib-rs`- this implementation utilizes the`zlib-rs`crate, a Rust rewrite of zlib. This backend is the fastest, at the cost of some`unsafe`Rust code.

Several backends implemented in C are also available. These are useful in case you are already using a specific C implementation and need the result of compression to be bit-identical. See the crate’s README for details on the available C backends.

The `zlib-rs` backend typically outperforms all the C implementations.

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature Flags

- `miniz_oxide`- *(enabled by default)*— This implementation uses only safe Rust code and doesn’t require a C compiler. It provides good performance for most use cases while being completely portable.
- `default`

[§](https://docs.rs#user-facing-backend-features)User-Facing Backend Features

Choose one of these features to select the compression backend.
Only one backend should be enabled at a time, or else one will see an unstable order which is currently
`zlib-ng`, `zlib-rs`, `cloudflare_zlib`, `miniz_oxide` and which may change at any time.

-
`rust_backend`*(enabled by default)*— Use the pure Rust`miniz_oxide`backend (default). This implementation uses only safe Rust code and doesn’t require a C compiler. It provides good performance for most use cases while being completely portable.Note that this feature at some point may be switched to use `zlib-rs`instead.
-
`zlib-rs``unsafe`code. It does not require a C compiler but uses`unsafe`Rust for optimization.
-
`miniz_oxide`*(enabled by default)*— Use the pure Rust`miniz_oxide`backend.
-
`zlib`
-
`zlib-default``zlib`but enables additional features from libz-sys.
-
`zlib-ng-compat``zlib-ng`feature. When using this feature, if any crate in your dependency graph explicitly requests stock zlib, or uses libz-sys directly without`default-features = false`, you’ll get stock zlib rather than zlib-ng. See[the libz-sys README](https://github.com/rust-lang/libz-sys/blob/main/README.md)for details. To avoid that, use the`"zlib-ng"`feature instead.
-
`zlib-ng`
-
`cloudflare_zlib`- ⚠ Does not support 32-bit CPUs and is incompatible with mingw.
- ⚠ May cause conflicts if other crates use different zlib versions.

-
`miniz-sys``rust_backend`, provided for backwards compatibility. Use`rust_backend`instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#internal-features)Internal Features

These features are used internally for backend selection and should not be enabled directly by users. They are documented here to aid with maintenance.

- `any_zlib`- **Internal:**Marker feature indicating that any zlib-based C backend is enabled. This is automatically enabled by- `zlib-rs`,- `zlib`,- `zlib-ng`,- `zlib-ng-compat`, and- `cloudflare_zlib`. Do not enable this feature directly; instead, choose a specific backend feature.
- `any_c_zlib`- **Internal:**Marker feature indicating that any C based fully zlib compatible backend is enabled. This is automatically enabled by- `zlib`,- `zlib-ng`,- `zlib-ng-compat`, and- `cloudflare_zlib`. Do not enable this feature directly; instead, choose a specific backend feature.
- `any_impl`- *(enabled by default)*—- **Internal:**Marker feature indicating that any compression backend is enabled. This is automatically enabled by all backend features to ensure at least one implementation is available. Do not enable this feature directly; instead, choose a specific backend feature.

[§](https://docs.rs#ambiguous-feature-selection)Ambiguous feature selection

As Cargo features are additive, while backends are not, there is an order in which backends become active if multiple are selected.

- zlib-ng
- zlib-rs
- cloudflare_zlib
- miniz_oxide

[§](https://docs.rs#organization)Organization

This crate consists of three main modules: `bufread`, `read`, and `write`. Each module
implements DEFLATE, zlib, and gzip for [ std::io::BufRead](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.BufRead.html) input types,

[input types, and](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.Read.html)

`std::io::Read`[output types respectively.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.Write.html)

`std::io::Write`Use the [ bufread](https://docs.rs/bufread/index.html) implementations if you can provide a

`BufRead` type for the input.
The `&[u8]` slice type implements the `BufRead` trait.The [ read](https://docs.rs/read/index.html) implementations conveniently wrap a

`Read` type in a `BufRead` implementation.
However, the `read` implementations may
[read past the end of the input data](https://github.com/rust-lang/flate2-rs/issues/338), making the

`Read` type useless for subsequent reads of the input. If you need to re-use the
`Read` type, wrap it in a [, use the](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/buffered/bufreader/struct.BufReader.html)

`std::io::BufReader``bufread` implementations,
and perform subsequent reads on the `BufReader`.The [ write](https://docs.rs/write/index.html) implementations are most useful when there is no way to create a

`BufRead`
type, notably when reading async iterators (streams).```
use futures::{Stream, StreamExt};
use std::io::{Result, Write as _};
async fn decompress_gzip_stream<S, I>(stream: S) -> Result<Vec<u8>>
where
    S: Stream<Item = I>,
    I: AsRef<[u8]>
{
    let mut stream = std::pin::pin!(stream);
    let mut w = Vec::<u8>::new();
    let mut decoder = flate2::write::GzDecoder::new(w);
    while let Some(input) = stream.next().await {
        decoder.write_all(input.as_ref())?;
    }
    decoder.finish()
}
```
Note that types which operate over a specific trait often implement the mirroring trait as well.
For example a `bufread::DeflateDecoder<T>` *also* implements the
[ Write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.Write.html) trait if

`T: Write`. That is, the “dual trait” is forwarded directly
to the underlying object if available.[§](https://docs.rs#about-multi-member-gzip-files)About multi-member Gzip files

While most `gzip` files one encounters will have a single *member* that can be read
with the [ GzDecoder](https://docs.rs/bufread/struct.GzDecoder.html), there may be some files which have multiple members.

A [ GzDecoder](https://docs.rs/bufread/struct.GzDecoder.html) will only read the first member of gzip data, which may unexpectedly
provide partial results when a multi-member gzip file is encountered.

`GzDecoder` is appropriate
for data that is designed to be read as single members from a multi-member file. `bufread::GzDecoder`
and `write::GzDecoder` also allow non-gzip data following gzip data to be handled.The [ MultiGzDecoder](https://docs.rs/bufread/struct.MultiGzDecoder.html) on the other hand will decode all members of a

`gzip` file
into one consecutive stream of bytes, which hides the underlying *members*entirely. If a file contains non-gzip data after the gzip data, MultiGzDecoder will emit an error after decoding the gzip data. This behavior matches the

`gzip`,
`gunzip`, and `zcat` command line tools.## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [bufread](https://docs.rs/bufread/index.html)
- Types which operate over `BufRead`
- [read](https://docs.rs/read/index.html)
- Types which operate over `Read`
- [write](https://docs.rs/write/index.html)
- Types which operate over `Write`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Compress](https://docs.rs/struct.Compress.html)
- Raw in-memory compression stream for blocks of data.
- [Compress](https://docs.rs/struct.CompressError.html)- Error
- Error returned when a compression object is used incorrectly or otherwise generates an error.
- [Compression](https://docs.rs/struct.Compression.html)
- When compressing data, the compression level can be specified by a value in this struct.
- [Crc](https://docs.rs/struct.Crc.html)- `zlib-rs`
- The CRC calculated by a `CrcReader`
- [CrcReader](https://docs.rs/struct.CrcReader.html)
- A wrapper around a `Read`
- [CrcWriter](https://docs.rs/struct.CrcWriter.html)
- A wrapper around a `Write`
- [Decompress](https://docs.rs/struct.Decompress.html)
- Raw in-memory decompression stream for blocks of data.
- [Decompress](https://docs.rs/struct.DecompressError.html)- Error
- Error returned when a decompression object finds that the input stream of bytes was not a valid input stream of bytes.
- [GzBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.GzBuilder.html)
- A builder structure to create a new gzip Encoder.
- [GzHeader](https://docs.rs/struct.GzHeader.html)
- A structure representing the header of a gzip stream.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Flush](https://docs.rs/enum.FlushCompress.html)- Compress
- Values which indicate the form of flushing to be used when compressing in-memory data.
- [Flush](https://docs.rs/enum.FlushDecompress.html)- Decompress
- Values which indicate the form of flushing to be used when decompressing in-memory data.
- [Status](https://docs.rs/enum.Status.html)
- Possible status results of compressing some data or successfully decompressing a block of data.

# plotters - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/plotters/^0.3.7/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#plotters---a-rust-drawing-library-focusing-on-data-plotting-for-both-wasm-and-native-applications-)Plotters - A Rust drawing library focusing on data plotting for both WASM and native applications 🦀📈🚀

Plotters is a drawing library designed for rendering figures, plots, and charts, in pure Rust. Plotters supports various types of back-ends, including bitmap, vector graph, piston window, GTK/Cairo and WebAssembly.

- A new Plotters Developer’s Guide is a work in progress. The preview version is available [here](https://plotters-rs.github.io/book).
- Try Plotters with an interactive Jupyter notebook, or view [here](https://plotters-rs.github.io/plotters-doc-data/evcxr-jupyter-integration.html)for the static HTML version.
- To view the WASM example, go to this [link](https://plotters-rs.github.io/wasm-demo/www/index.html)
- Currently we have all the internal code ready for console plotting, but a console based backend is still not ready. See [this example](https://github.com/plotters-rs/plotters/blob/master/plotters/examples/console.rs)for how to plot on console with a customized backend.
- Plotters has moved all backend code to separate repositories, check [FAQ list](https://docs.rs#faq-list)for details
- Some interesting [demo projects](https://docs.rs#demo-projects)are available, feel free to try them out.

[§](https://docs.rs#dependencies)Dependencies

[§](https://docs.rs#ubuntu-linux)Ubuntu Linux

`sudo apt install pkg-config libfreetype6-dev libfontconfig1-dev`

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick Start

To use Plotters, you can simply add Plotters into your `Cargo.toml`

```
[dependencies]
plotters = "0.3.3"
```
And the following code draws a quadratic function. `src/main.rs`,

```
use plotters::prelude::*;
fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let root = BitMapBackend::new("plotters-doc-data/0.png", (640, 480)).into_drawing_area();
    root.fill(&WHITE)?;
    let mut chart = ChartBuilder::on(&root)
        .caption("y=x^2", ("sans-serif", 50).into_font())
        .margin(5)
        .x_label_area_size(30)
        .y_label_area_size(30)
        .build_cartesian_2d(-1f32..1f32, -0.1f32..1f32)?;
    chart.configure_mesh().draw()?;
    chart
        .draw_series(LineSeries::new(
            (-50..=50).map(|x| x as f32 / 50.0).map(|x| (x, x * x)),
            &RED,
        ))?
        .label("y = x^2")
        .legend(|(x, y)| PathElement::new(vec![(x, y), (x + 20, y)], &RED));
    chart
        .configure_series_labels()
        .background_style(&WHITE.mix(0.8))
        .border_style(&BLACK)
        .draw()?;
    root.present()?;
    Ok(())
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#demo-projects)Demo Projects

To learn how to use Plotters in different scenarios, check out the following demo projects:

- WebAssembly + Plotters: [plotters-wasm-demo](https://github.com/plotters-rs/plotters-wasm-demo)
- minifb + Plotters: [plotters-minifb-demo](https://github.com/plotters-rs/plotters-minifb-demo)
- GTK + Plotters: [plotters-gtk-demo](https://github.com/plotters-rs/plotters-gtk-demo)

[§](https://docs.rs#trying-with-jupyter-evcxr-kernel-interactively)Trying with Jupyter evcxr Kernel Interactively

Plotters now supports integration with `evcxr` and is able to interactively draw plots in Jupyter Notebook.
The feature `evcxr` should be enabled when including Plotters to Jupyter Notebook.

The following code shows a minimal example of this.

```
:dep plotters = { version = "^0.3.6", default-features = false, features = ["evcxr", "all_series", "all_elements"] }
extern crate plotters;
use plotters::prelude::*;
let figure = evcxr_figure((640, 480), |root| {
    root.fill(&WHITE)?;
    let mut chart = ChartBuilder::on(&root)
        .caption("y=x^2", ("Arial", 50).into_font())
        .margin(5)
        .x_label_area_size(30)
        .y_label_area_size(30)
        .build_cartesian_2d(-1f32..1f32, -0.1f32..1f32)?;
    chart.configure_mesh().draw()?;
    chart.draw_series(LineSeries::new(
        (-50..=50).map(|x| x as f32 / 50.0).map(|x| (x, x * x)),
        &RED,
    )).unwrap()
        .label("y = x^2")
        .legend(|(x,y)| PathElement::new(vec![(x,y), (x + 20,y)], &RED));
    chart.configure_series_labels()
        .background_style(&WHITE.mix(0.8))
        .border_style(&BLACK)
        .draw()?;
    Ok(())
});
figure
```
[§](https://docs.rs#interactive-tutorial-with-jupyter-notebook)Interactive Tutorial with Jupyter Notebook

*This tutorial is a work in progress and isn’t complete*

Thanks to the evcxr, now we have an interactive tutorial for Plotters!
To use the interactive notebook, you must have Jupyter and evcxr installed on your computer.
Follow the instruction on [this page](https://github.com/google/evcxr/tree/master/evcxr_jupyter) below to install it.

After that, you should be able to start your Jupyter server locally and load the tutorial!

```
git clone https://github.com/38/plotters-doc-data
cd plotters-doc-data
jupyter notebook
```
And select the notebook called `evcxr-jupyter-integration.ipynb`.

Also, there’s a static HTML version of this notebook available at [this location](https://plotters-rs.github.io/plotters-doc-data/evcxr-jupyter-integration.html)

[§](https://docs.rs#plotting-in-rust)Plotting in Rust

Rust is a perfect language for data visualization. Although there are many mature visualization libraries in many different languages, Rust is one of the best languages that fits the need.

-
**Easy to use**Rust has a very good iterator system built into the standard library. With the help of iterators, plotting in Rust can be as easy as most of the high-level programming languages. The Rust based plotting library can be very easy to use.
-
**Fast**If you need to render a figure with trillions of data points, Rust is a good choice. Rust’s performance allows you to combine the data processing step and rendering step into a single application. When plotting in high-level programming languages, e.g. Javascript or Python, data points must be down-sampled before feeding into the plotting program because of the performance considerations. Rust is fast enough to do the data processing and visualization within a single program. You can also integrate the figure rendering code into your application to handle a huge amount of data and visualize it in real-time.
-
**WebAssembly Support**Rust is one of the languages with the best WASM support. Plotting in Rust could be very useful for visualization on a web page and would have a huge performance improvement comparing to Javascript.

[§](https://docs.rs#plotting-on-html5-canvas-with-wasm-backend)Plotting on HTML5 canvas with WASM Backend

Plotters currently supports a backend that uses the HTML5 canvas. To use WASM, you can simply use
`CanvasBackend` instead of other backend and all other API remains the same!

There’s a small demo for Plotters + WASM available at [here](https://github.com/plotters-rs/plotters-wasm-demo).
To play with the deployed version, follow this [link](https://plotters-rs.github.io/wasm-demo/www/index.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#what-types-of-figure-are-supported)What types of figure are supported?

Plotters is not limited to any specific type of figure. You can create your own types of figures easily with the Plotters API.

Plotters does provide some built-in figure types for convenience. Currently, we support line series, point series, candlestick series, and histogram. And the library is designed to be able to render multiple figure into a single image. But Plotter is aimed to be a platform that is fully extendable to support any other types of figure.

[§](https://docs.rs#concepts-by-example)Concepts by example

[§](https://docs.rs#drawing-backends)Drawing Backends

Plotters can use different drawing backends, including SVG, BitMap, and even real-time rendering. For example, a bitmap drawing backend.

```
use plotters::prelude::*;
fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    // Create a 800*600 bitmap and start drawing
    let mut backend = BitMapBackend::new("plotters-doc-data/1.png", (300, 200));
    // And if we want SVG backend
    // let backend = SVGBackend::new("output.svg", (800, 600));
    backend.draw_rect((50, 50), (200, 150), &RED, true)?;
    backend.present()?;
    Ok(())
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#drawing-area)Drawing Area

Plotters uses a concept called drawing area for layout purpose. Plotters supports integrating multiple figures into a single image. This is done by creating sub-drawing-areas.

Besides that, the drawing area also allows for a customized coordinate system, by doing so, the coordinate mapping is done by the drawing area automatically.

```
use plotters::prelude::*;
fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let root_drawing_area =
        BitMapBackend::new("plotters-doc-data/2.png", (300, 200)).into_drawing_area();
    // And we can split the drawing area into 3x3 grid
    let child_drawing_areas = root_drawing_area.split_evenly((3, 3));
    // Then we fill the drawing area with different color
    for (area, color) in child_drawing_areas.into_iter().zip(0..) {
        area.fill(&Palette99::pick(color))?;
    }
    root_drawing_area.present()?;
    Ok(())
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#elements)Elements

In Plotters, elements are the building blocks of figures. All elements are able to be drawn on a drawing area. There are different types of built-in elements, like lines, texts, circles, etc. You can also define your own element in the application code.

You may also combine existing elements to build a complex element.

To learn more about the element system, please read the [element module documentation](https://docs.rs/element/index.html).

```
use plotters::prelude::*;
fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let root = BitMapBackend::new("plotters-doc-data/3.png", (300, 200)).into_drawing_area();
    root.fill(&WHITE)?;
    // Draw an circle on the drawing area
    root.draw(&Circle::new(
        (100, 100),
        50,
        Into::<ShapeStyle>::into(&GREEN).filled(),
    ))?;
    root.present()?;
    Ok(())
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#composable-elements)Composable Elements

Besides the built-in elements, elements can be composed into a logical group we called composed elements.
When composing new elements, the upper-left corner is given in the target coordinate, and a new pixel-based
coordinate which has the upper-left corner defined as `(0,0)` is used for further element composition.

For example, we can have an element which includes a dot and its coordinate.

```
use plotters::prelude::*;
use plotters::coord::types::RangedCoordf32;
fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let root = BitMapBackend::new("plotters-doc-data/4.png", (640, 480)).into_drawing_area();
    root.fill(&RGBColor(240, 200, 200))?;
    let root = root.apply_coord_spec(Cartesian2d::<RangedCoordf32, RangedCoordf32>::new(
        0f32..1f32,
        0f32..1f32,
        (0..640, 0..480),
    ));
    let dot_and_label = |x: f32, y: f32| {
        return EmptyElement::at((x, y))
            + Circle::new((0, 0), 3, ShapeStyle::from(&BLACK).filled())
            + Text::new(
                format!("({:.2},{:.2})", x, y),
                (10, 0),
                ("sans-serif", 15.0).into_font(),
            );
    };
    root.draw(&dot_and_label(0.5, 0.6))?;
    root.draw(&dot_and_label(0.25, 0.33))?;
    root.draw(&dot_and_label(0.8, 0.8))?;
    root.present()?;
    Ok(())
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#chart-context)Chart Context

In order to draw a chart, Plotters needs a data object built on top of the drawing area called `ChartContext`.
The chart context defines even higher level constructs compare to the drawing area.
For example, you can define the label areas, meshes, and put a data series onto the drawing area with the help
of the chart context object.

```
use plotters::prelude::*;
fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let root = BitMapBackend::new("plotters-doc-data/5.png", (640, 480)).into_drawing_area();
    root.fill(&WHITE);
    let root = root.margin(10, 10, 10, 10);
    // After this point, we should be able to construct a chart context
    let mut chart = ChartBuilder::on(&root)
        // Set the caption of the chart
        .caption("This is our first plot", ("sans-serif", 40).into_font())
        // Set the size of the label region
        .x_label_area_size(20)
        .y_label_area_size(40)
        // Finally attach a coordinate on the drawing area and make a chart context
        .build_cartesian_2d(0f32..10f32, 0f32..10f32)?;
    // Then we can draw a mesh
    chart
        .configure_mesh()
        // We can customize the maximum number of labels allowed for each axis
        .x_labels(5)
        .y_labels(5)
        // We can also change the format of the label text
        .y_label_formatter(&|x| format!("{:.3}", x))
        .draw()?;
    // And we can draw something in the drawing area
    chart.draw_series(LineSeries::new(
        vec![(0.0, 0.0), (5.0, 5.0), (8.0, 7.0)],
        &RED,
    ))?;
    // Similarly, we can draw point series
    chart.draw_series(PointSeries::of_element(
        vec![(0.0, 0.0), (5.0, 5.0), (8.0, 7.0)],
        5,
        &RED,
        &|c, s, st| {
            return EmptyElement::at(c)    // We want to construct a composed element on-the-fly
            + Circle::new((0,0),s,st.filled()) // At this point, the new pixel coordinate is established
            + Text::new(format!("{:?}", c), (10, 0), ("sans-serif", 10).into_font());
        },
    ))?;
    root.present()?;
    Ok(())
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#misc)Misc

[§](https://docs.rs#development-version)Development Version

Find the latest development version of Plotters on [GitHub](https://github.com/plotters-rs/plotters.git).
Clone the repository and learn more about the Plotters API and ways to contribute. Your help is needed!

If you want to add the development version of Plotters to your project, add the following to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[dependencies]
plotters = { git = "https://github.com/plotters-rs/plotters.git" }
```
[§](https://docs.rs#reducing-depending-libraries--turning-off-backends)Reducing Depending Libraries && Turning Off Backends

Plotters now supports use features to control the backend dependencies. By default, `BitMapBackend` and `SVGBackend` are supported,
use `default-features = false` in the dependency description in `Cargo.toml` and you can cherry-pick the backend implementations.

- `svg`Enable the- `SVGBackend`
- `bitmap`Enable the- `BitMapBackend`

For example, the following dependency description would avoid compiling with bitmap support:

```
[dependencies]
plotters = { git = "https://github.com/plotters-rs/plotters.git", default-features = false, features = ["svg"] }
```
The library also allows consumers to make use of the [ Palette](https://crates.io/crates/palette/) crate’s color types by default.
This behavior can also be turned off by setting

`default-features = false`.[§](https://docs.rs#list-of-features)List of Features

This is the full list of features that is defined by `Plotters` crate.
Use `default-features = false` to disable those default enabled features,
and then you should be able to cherry-pick what features you want to include into `Plotters` crate.
By doing so, you can minimize the number of dependencies down to only `itertools` and compile time is less than 6s.

The following list is a complete list of features that can be opted in or out.

- Tier 1 drawing backends

| Name | Description | Additional Dependency | Default? |
|---|---|---|---|
| bitmap_encoder | Allow `BitMapBackend`to save the result to bitmap files | image, rusttype, font-kit | Yes |
| svg_backend | Enable `SVGBackend`Support | None | Yes |
| bitmap_gif | Opt-in GIF animation Rendering support for `BitMapBackend`, implies`bitmap`enabled | gif | Yes |

- Font manipulation features

| Name | Description | Additional Dependency | Default? |
|---|---|---|---|
| ttf | Allows TrueType font support | font-kit | Yes |
| ab_glyph | Skips loading system fonts, unlike `ttf` | ab_glyph | No |

`ab_glyph` supports TrueType and OpenType fonts, but does not attempt to
load fonts provided by the system on which it is running.
It is pure Rust, and easier to cross compile.
To use this, you *must* call `plotters::style::register_font` before
using any `plotters` functions which require the ability to render text.
This function only exists when the `ab_glyph` feature is enabled.

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
/// Register a font in the fonts table.
///
/// The `name` parameter gives the name this font shall be referred to
/// in the other APIs, like `"sans-serif"`.
///
/// Unprovided font styles for a given name will fallback to `FontStyle::Normal`
/// if that is available for that name, when other functions lookup fonts which
/// are registered with this function.
///
/// The `bytes` parameter should be the complete contents
/// of an OpenType font file, like:
/// ```ignore
/// include_bytes!("FiraGO-Regular.otf")
/// ```
pub fn register_font(
    name: &str,
    style: FontStyle,
    bytes: &'static [u8],
) -> Result<(), InvalidFont>
```
- Coordinate features

| Name | Description | Additional Dependency | Default? |
|---|---|---|---|
| datetime | Enable the date and time coordinate support | chrono | Yes |

- Element, series and util functions

| Name | Description | Additional Dependency | Default? |
|---|---|---|---|
| errorbar | The errorbar element support | None | Yes |
| candlestick | The candlestick element support | None | Yes |
| boxplot | The boxplot element support | None | Yes |
| area_series | The area series support | None | Yes |
| line_series | The line series support | None | Yes |
| histogram | The histogram series support | None | Yes |
| point_series | The point series support | None | Yes |

- Misc

| Name | Description | Additional Dependency | Default? |
|---|---|---|---|
| deprecated_items | This feature allows use of deprecated items which is going to be removed in the future | None | Yes |
| debug | Enable the code used for debugging | None | No |

[§](https://docs.rs#faq-list)FAQ List

-
Why does the WASM example break on my machine ? The WASM example requires using `wasm32`target to build. Using`cargo build`is likely to use the default target which in most of the case is any of the x86 target. Thus you need add`--target=wasm32-unknown-unknown`in the cargo parameter list to build it.
-
How to draw text/circle/point/rectangle/… on the top of chart ? As you may have realized, Plotters is a drawing library rather than a traditional data plotting library, you have the freedom to draw anything you want on the drawing area. Use `DrawingArea::draw`to draw any element on the drawing area.
-
Where can I find the backend code ? Since Plotters 0.3, all drawing backends are independent crate from the main Plotters crate. Use the following link to find the backend code:
-
How to check if a backend writes to a file successfully ? The behavior of Plotters backend is consistent with the standard library. When the backend instance is dropped, `crate::drawing::DrawingArea::present()``Backend::present()`is called automatically whenever is needed. When the`present()`method is called from`drop`, any error will be silently ignored.In the case that error handling is important, you need manually call the `present()`method before the backend gets dropped. For more information, please see the examples.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [backend](https://docs.rs/backend/index.html)
- This module contains some useful re-export of backend related types.
- [chart](https://docs.rs/chart/index.html)
- The high-level plotting abstractions.
- [coord](https://docs.rs/coord/index.html)
- One of the key features of Plotters is flexible coordinate system abstraction and this module provides all the abstraction used for the coordinate abstraction of Plotters.
- [data](https://docs.rs/data/index.html)
- The data processing module, which implements algorithms related to visualization of data. Such as, down-sampling, etc.
- [drawing](https://docs.rs/drawing/index.html)
- The drawing utils for Plotters. In Plotters, we have two set of drawing APIs: low-level API and high-level API.
- [element](https://docs.rs/element/index.html)
- Defines the drawing elements, the high-level drawing unit in Plotters drawing system
- [evcxr](https://docs.rs/evcxr/index.html)- `evcxr`
- Evaluation Context for Rust. See [the evcxr crate](https://crates.io/crates/evcxr)for more information.
- [prelude](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)
- The module imports the most commonly used types and modules in Plotters
- [series](https://docs.rs/series/index.html)
- This module contains predefined types of series.
The series in Plotters is actually an iterator of elements, which
can be taken by `ChartContext::draw_series`function.
- [style](https://docs.rs/style/index.html)
- The style for shapes and text, font, color, etc.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [define_](https://docs.rs/macro.define_color.html)- color
- Defines and names a color based on its R, G, B, A values.
- [doc](https://docs.rs/macro.doc.html)
- Macro for allowing dynamic creation of doc attributes.

# nn_rust - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/nn_rust/0.1.0/target-redirect/nn_rust/

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use neural_net::network::`- [Network](https://docs.rs/neural_net/network/struct.Network.html);
- `pub use neural_net::data_point::`- [DataPoint](https://docs.rs/neural_net/data_point/struct.DataPoint.html);
- `pub use neural_net::matrix::`- [Vector](https://docs.rs/neural_net/matrix/struct.Vector.html);
